free_tier.stated: Unlimited total: 'The total volume and number of your files are unlimited'. Free unregistered uploads are capped at 200 MB; registered free accounts go much higher (operator advertises up to 100 GB file transfer volume).

per_object_cap.stated: file size ceiling well above 200 MB

egress.terms: Free downloads: ~5 GB/day per user with a hard speed cap and IP queueing. Turbo: 40 GB/day and 600 GB/month. No per-GB price.

record.tooling: Turbobit Uploader desktop app, FTP upload, and third-party rclone/JDownloader support; no first-party public REST API documented.
record.chaining: Unlimited total per account is the headline; with email-only registration the chain is N accounts. The 40 GB/day cap is per download identity, so serving volume scales with IPs, not accounts.

limits.value: file size ceiling well above 200 MB

record.limits_note: Registered free: file size ceiling well above 200 MB (unregistered 200 MB). Retention: files expire after inactivity ('storage time expiration' is a listed deletion reason). Free download ~5 GB/day, 55-60 KB/s class throttling on the sister host. Turbo 40 GB/day, 600 GB/month.
record.reliability_note: Free-tier serving is throttled to dial-up speeds and gated behind a human-verification step and a queue, so it works as storage but not as a fetch origin. Dyna mic Download Splitting means the previous file's size sets your next wait.

evidence.proved: 'Store as many files as you want — The total volume and number of your files are unlimited'
'If you are a free user, you may download about 5 Gb a day'; Turbo '40 Gb a day, 600 Gb per month'; 'storage time expiration' is a deletion reason
